svg.title: A client has endometritis 48 hr after a cesarean birth. Which finding should the nurse anticipate? Normal: WBC can reach 20,000 to 25,000/mm³ after birth
svg.desc: Tachycardia is the one to expect. Fever drives the pulse up, and it stands out all the more after a birth, because the normal postpartum pulse runs slow — puerperal bradycardia — so 110/min is a long way from where it should be. It travels with chills, fatigue, anorexia, pelvic pain, a tender uterus and foul-smelling lochia . The trap is judging the other three against non-pregnant ranges. A white count of 8,000/mm³ looks normal, but ordinary postpartum leukocytosis runs 20,000–25,000/mm³ in the first days, so 8,000 is below what this client should have — which is also why a white count is a poor infection marker in this first week. The ESR is normally raised in pregnancy and the puerperium, so 15 mm/hr is unremarkable too. Respirations of 18/min are simply normal.
